Outputs: root pointer $02/$03 and renderer bounds/depth/offset state are initialized; recursive records are traversed and their leaves update bitmap, screen, and color work memory
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, recursive stack use, scene pointers and renderer scratch including $02/$03, $0A, $1A/$1B, $38, $DC, and $E7
Hardware: directly writes VIC-II background color $D021; the leaf renderer at $8690 writes the bitmap, screen RAM, colour RAM and the colour copy at $0800 itself; only for a cell whose colour copy already has bits 5-7 set does it look further, leaving the cell alone when the new colour byte is below $20 and calling the resident compositor ($1411, which jumps to $17F6) when that byte has bit 4 set

Render room A in the Street playable phase, entering the normal scene renderer after its usual load from $A2.
Inputs: A is a valid room index; relocated scene pointers, renderer workspace, bitmap/screen/color buffers, and the active phase are initialized.
Outputs: Selects the room's scene pointer, writes its background color to $D021, traverses the scene-record tree, and renders the room.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02-$05, renderer scratch, and VIC-II-visible bitmap/screen/color work memory.
Hardware: Writes VIC-II background-color register $D021 and display memory; no CIA access.

Interpret and render a scene-record tree. Inputs: $02/$03 record pointer and initialized renderer workspace. Outputs: bitmap, screen, color, and traversal state are updated. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and renderer zero-page scratch. Hardware: changes hardware-visible bitmap, screen, and color RAM; no direct VIC-II register write is required.

Dispatch the current encoded scene record for the Street playable phase, restoring a parent record at nested terminators and returning at the outer terminator.
Inputs: $02/$03 point at the current record; $1A/$1B hold the composite origin; $38 is nesting depth; nested parent frames are on the stack.
Outputs: Decodes nonterminal records; $FF at depth zero returns, while nested $FF restores the parent frame, advances $02/$03, and continues dispatch.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02-$05, $1A/$1B, $25/$26, $38, renderer scratch, and restored stack bytes.
Hardware: No direct register write here; descendant rendering changes VIC-II-visible bitmap, screen-code, and color memory.

Advance over the current Street playable-phase scene record and resume the scene-record dispatch loop.
Inputs: $02/$03 point at a valid encoded record with length/control bits in bytes +1 and +2.
Outputs: Adds the record's encoded length to $02/$03 and tail-jumps back to scene dispatch.
Clobbers: A, Y, N, V, Z, C, and $02/$03; X is preserved.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes; when subsequent records render, the resumed renderer updates VIC-II-visible display memory.
Advance $02/$03 to the next encoded scene record. Inputs: $02/$03 points at a valid record header. Outputs: $02/$03 points at the following record. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, and $02/$03.

Decode and render the nonterminal Street playable-phase scene record at $02/$03, including nested composite records.
Inputs: $02/$03 point at a non-$FF record; $1A/$1B hold its origin; relocated scene-pointer tables and renderer buffers are initialized.
Outputs: Decodes position/reflection fields, resolves child or leaf pointers, renders the record, and advances or resumes the enclosing scene tree.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02-$05, $1A/$1B, $25/$26, $38, renderer scratch, and nesting stack state.
Hardware: No CIA access; descendant rendering changes VIC-II-visible bitmap, screen-code, and color memory.

Draw the picture (scene leaf) that $04/$05 point at, for the Street playable phase: every leaf of a scene tree falls into it from $8684-$868E, and DrawUiImageRecord jumps to it at $AD2C to draw a status-panel picture.
Inputs: $04/$05 point at the picture (first byte width and height nibbles, then its bitmap, screen and colour bytes); $25/$26 hold its column and row and $E8 bit 7 mirrors it; $E7/$DC are the clipping width and height; $02/$03 point at the record that placed it, whose byte 2 bits 5-6 give the number of colour-swap bytes that follow byte 2.
Outputs: Draws the visible cells into the bitmap, screen RAM, colour RAM and the colour copy at $0800, with the colour swaps applied; a picture wholly outside the window is skipped. Then it jumps to AdvanceSceneRecordAndContinue ($85F8), which steps $02/$03 past the placing record and resumes the scene-record dispatch loop.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02-$09, coordinate/renderer scratch, and display work memory.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register write; it stores the bitmap, screen-code and colour bytes itself, and calls the resident compositor at $1411 for cells whose colours must be merged.

Bootstrap Street scene, object, display, and interrupt state before gameplay setup; it builds no collision data, which CompileCollision ($B233) compiles later, from $8A6B
Inputs: resident renderer/IRQ services and the active Street tables and workspaces
Outputs: clears $0230, initializes scene/object work through $8D18/$8DF1/$8F2B/$91CE, sets $02A8=$FF and $C0=$FF, configures the bitmap display, and transfers through the resident IRQ-install tail
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and all scratch/state used by the five called initializers and resident IRQ setup
Hardware: ScreenSetupVeneer programs VIC-II display registers; the tail at $1533 installs VIC/CIA IRQ state and resident vectors

Clear the play window and render The Street's credit/title card from six inline records. Inputs: resident play-window clear routine $140E and inline-record renderer $1583 are active; six well-formed inline records follow their calls. Outputs: the credit/title card is displayed and $7B is set to $BF. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $7B, and renderer scratch. Hardware: changes visible display memory through resident helpers.

EngineEntry: The Street's play code starts here, from PhaseHandoff at $3FF3. It sets $AA to $FF, which lets the interrupt routine play the tune, relocates the scene pointers, clears the scene buffers, waits 25 ticks, lowers the sprite curtain over the play window (AnimateStatusPanelReveal, $1F75), draws the credits card, sets the background to black, raises the curtain again and waits until it is gone (RaiseSpriteCurtain, $8CA2), which shows the card, then waits for the fire button or the second button read through the SID's pot X ($D419), keeping which in $AC, and goes on into EnterArea ($8A3D) and the main loop. Central Park's EngineEntry also sets $03CB to 1; this one leaves it alone.

Reinitialize the Street playable phase's scene buffers after GAME OVER and rejoin engine startup immediately before the common gameplay-entry tail. Its one caller is $8B94, reached when the last life is lost and no spare life is left.
Inputs: The death sequence has finished; resident state and the active phase occupant remain valid.
Outputs: Calls the phase scene-buffer initializer, clears $D021 to black, redraws the credit/title card (RenderCreditTitleCard, $894E, which clears the play window first), and continues at the engine's input/frame-loop setup at $8A22.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, scene/gameplay initialization state, and helper scratch.
Hardware: Writes VIC-II background color $D021 and updates display/input state through the joined engine-start tail.

Set up the current area and enter the main loop, for The Street. This runs once each time an area is entered or redrawn, not once a frame: it is reached by falling through from the start-up wait at $8A3B, from MainTick when the redraw latch $02A9 is set ($8AF0), after a lost life ($8B57) and after a declined level exit ($8C9F), and it falls into MainTick ($8A9A), the per-tick loop.
Inputs: Current area $A2, the player's position and the actor/object state.
Outputs: Sets $0230=$7F; rebuilds the area's enemy meter when $012D,X holds $80-$FE and loads $022A from the area's enemy energy at $3F92; clears the play window and draws the area's scene ($91EF); draws the crossing light of the areas that have one (1, 4, 5, 8, 9 and 11), red or green by the light state $03EA (DrawCrossingLight, $9A4E, a call The Street adds); clears the actor slots, resets runtime state, compiles the collision records, spawns the enemy, draws inactive objects and composes the actors; on the first visit to an area below $12 sets its $011B byte and adds a score bonus ($1183 with A=$15); redraws the HUD digits, applies the area's entrance rules ($912E), stamps $026D from $E2, sets $0230=$FF and falls into MainTick.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $0230, gameplay zero page, actor/object/projectile arrays, renderer/collision scratch, and display work state.
Hardware: Through its helpers, writes $D021 and the VIC-II-visible bitmap, screen and colour memory.
The Street's own RenderConditionalSceneVariant ($91EF): the plain scene, never a variant
The Street adds this call: draw the crossing light, if the area has one

Admit one IRQ-produced tick, run the Street gameplay scheduler in fixed order, and choose the next engine transition
Inputs: IRQ tick $E2 and last stamp $0268; initialized player, enemy, script, event, object, projectile, scene, and transition state
Outputs: stamps $0268; runs timing/input, player, AI, enemy animation, events, scripts, level conditions, objects, boundaries, projectiles, presentation, and resident services; then loops, restarts setup, enters death handling, or begins the level transition
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and the union of all scheduled subsystem scratch/state
The Street's own ServiceEnemyBoundaryLatch, for the traps in areas 5 and 7
The Street adds this call to advance the crossing lights; Central Park has no call here

Resolve the player's death in The Street, present the result, and select restart or GAME OVER flow. MainTick comes here when $B4 is set ($8AE6); the level exit ($02AF) goes to ResolveLevelCompletion ($8B97), which MainTick jumps to directly
Inputs: death latch $B4, lives $03F2, spare-life flag $03E0 (item 8) and selected object $0279
Outputs: sets $0230=$7F and clears $B4, $B3 and $B6; clears the inactive-object display; LoseLife takes one from the lives; with lives left shows 'N LIVES LEFT' or '1 LIFE REMAINING' (counting the spare life), restores health, reloads the selected spawn and restarts at $8A3D; with none left spends the spare life if it is held, otherwise renders GAME OVER and restarts the level through ResetSceneAfterDeath ($8A17)
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and renderer, delay, object and spawn scratch
Hardware: sets $D021=0 through LoseLife ($8F1D); other display changes occur through called resident/level helpers

Text "0 LIVES LEFT", drawn by the call at $8B1D that comes before it: column 9, row 8, colours $07 and $C0, then 12 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The 0 at $8B24 is a placeholder: the instruction at $8B1A writes the lives left (counting the spare life) plus $1B into it before the call, so the line reads 2 LIVES LEFT or more. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $8B31.

The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "0 LIVES LEFT" at $8B30, and the routine that called it at $8B1D goes on.

ResolveLevelCompletion: runs when the completion request $02AF is set. It looks up each of the 2 items listed at $91F4 (1, 10) in the item flags at $03D8. With one missing it asks ARE YOU SURE YOU ARE PREPARED FOR THE NEXT LEVEL, YES or NO, and NO returns the player to the level. Then it adds 5,000 points to the score ($1183 with A = $50: 5 to the thousands digit, 0 to the hundreds), takes away item 11 (clears $03E3), saves the items, score and clock for the next level (SaveLevelState, $1C30), counts the energy $0229 up from 0 to 21, one step each time the interrupt routine changes $022B, and jumps to the load coordinator at $16AD for the next part.

Text "ARE YOU SURE", drawn by the call at $8BD8 that comes before it: column 9, row 5, colours $07 and $C0, then 12 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $8BEC.

Raise the sprite curtain over the play window and wait until it is gone. Inputs: $0232 is the curtain's lower edge (a raster line, which AnimateStatusPanelReveal at $1F75 lowered) and the interrupt owns the $0231 handshake. Outputs: $0232 is reduced, two lines a frame, below $1D, sprite X expansion is disabled and $0231 is cleared, so the interrupt stops drawing the curtain. Called at the start of the game ($8A11), after a lost life ($8B51) and after GAME OVER ($8B8C). Clobbers: A, flags, $0231, and $0232. Hardware: writes VIC-II sprite X-expansion register $D01D.

Reset mutable Street engine state each time an area is set up: its one caller is $8A68, in the area set-up routine that also runs at the start of play and after a lost life. Inputs: the active overlay and resident reset service. Outputs: timers, actor and object flags, arrays, and sentinels are restored to initial values. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and broad engine state. Hardware: none; the resident call (ResetEngineTickBaselines, $11F1) only copies the tick $E2 into $026C, $026E and $0277, and this body makes no direct I/O write.

Set up the status of a level as it starts. It clears $022B, $022C, $70, $89 and $A0, fills the 30 bytes at $3F92 that keep each area's enemy energy, and both energies ($0229, $022A) with $2C, a full bar, and sets $7A to $90. It copies the item flags saved when the level began ($03B0-$03D7) over the live ones ($03D8-$03FF) and clears $03E9-$03F1 among them, then puts the score ($1CA0) and the clock's digits back from the saved copy ($03CC-$03D7). It sets $87 to $B8, clears $011B-$013E and draws panel picture 0 at both of its places (DrawUiImageRecord, $ACFC, with A = 0 and X = 0, then 1). It builds no scene or wall data. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and the drawing routine's scratch.

Take the exit at the edge of the current area; MainTick calls it once a tick, and it does nothing while $0234 is non-zero. Inputs: $0234, current area $A2, player position $54 (across) and $55 (down), and the exit thresholds at $8E41. Outputs: when the player is at an edge (Y below 9, Y $BD or more, X $F7 or more, or X below 2) the position becomes a place on the area's edge, counted clockwise from the top left: a quarter of the distance along the edge, plus 0 on the top, $3D on the right, $6A on the bottom and $A7 on the left. The first exit of the area's group in $8E41 whose threshold is above that place is installed through InstallSceneStateRecordX ($8DF3), which moves the player to the destination area and position, or sets the level-exit request $02AF=$FF when the destination is $FF. Away from the edges it returns without change. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and the installed area/player state.

Install record 0, the level's starting place, as the selected spawn: it loads X with 0 and falls into InstallSceneStateRecordX, whatever the current room. In Street record 0 is area 1 at X $58, Y $5A, heading 3. Its one caller is InitSceneBuffers ($893B). Inputs: none. Outputs: $0278=0, and the area, player position, heading, command and redraw latches from record 0. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and the installed area/player state.

Install the Street scene-state/spawn record selected by X.
Inputs: X indexes parallel area, player-coordinate, heading, and command-state arrays at $8E69/$8E91/$8EB9/$8EE1; callers have already resolved the transition variant and any $0234 gate.
Outputs: A $FF area byte sets $02AF=$FF and returns; otherwise stores X in $0278 and installs area $A2, player coordinates $54/$55/$028E/$028F/$74, heading $68/$69, derived pose $65, command $81, and redraw latches $02A9/$02B8.
Clobbers: A, X, processor flags, $0278, $02AF on the sentinel path, and the installed area/player/redraw state; Y is preserved.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Load the selected Street spawn record into active area, player-position, facing, and transition state
Inputs: $0278 = selected record index; parallel Street area, X, Y, and packed facing/state tables
Outputs: $A2 = area; $54/$028E = X; $55/$74/$028F = Y; $68/$69 = heading; $65 = $10 or $11 facing-image selector; $81 = packed byte shifted right four; $02A9/$02B8 = $FF; A = $FF; X = selected index
Clobbers: A, X, and processor flags; Y is preserved

40 bytes of exit thresholds. Byte 0 belongs to no area: the scans start at byte 1, and entry 0 of the four tables that follow is the level's start position. Then comes a group for each area, closed by $FF. The routine that finds the exit the player is walking through skips a group for each area before the current one, turns the player's place on the edge of the play window into one number running clockwise round it from the top left, and takes the first value in the group above that number, the closing $FF included. The same index then selects the exit's destination in the four tables that follow.

40 exits, $8E69-$8E90: the area it leads to, or $FF for the way out of the level (entry 38, the closing $FF of area 14's group), which sets the level-exit request $02AF instead of moving the player. Values: 0, 12, 1, 2, 13, 2, 4, 0, 14, 0, 1, 4, 15, 1, 5, 3, 6, 4, 7, 9, 5, 8, 6, 11, 7, 6, 12, 11, 8, 10, 9, 13, 0, 14, 1, 12, 2, 13, 255, 3.

40 exits, $8EE1-$8F08: the heading in the low three bits, and a command in the high nibble. Values: 5, 1, 3, 7, 1, 3, 5, 7, 1, 3, 7, 3, 7, 1, 3, 7, 3, 7, 3, 5, 7, 3, 7, 5, 7, 1, 5, 3, 1, 7, 1, 3, 5, 3, 5, 7, 5, 7, 255, 3.

The player's death, once the fall is over: it clears $F2, crumbles the sprites away (DissolveSpriteImages, $AD35), lowers the sprite curtain over the play window again (AnimateStatusPanelReveal, $1F75), waits 25 ticks (WaitEngineTicks, $A25E), clears the play window ($140E), sets the background to black and takes one from the lives, item 26's flag at $03F2. The caller tests the Z flag that the DEC leaves: with no lives left it spends a spare life, item 8, if the player has one, and otherwise the game is over. Clobbers: A, X, Y and flags.
Impose a short fixed CPU delay. Inputs: none. Outputs: X ends at zero after 128 countdown iterations. Clobbers: X and flags; A and Y are preserved.

Reset The Street's transient control, actor, object, animation, and AI state to its fixed entry sentinels when the level starts or restarts: its one caller is InitSceneBuffers ($8942), not the area set-up. Inputs: No register arguments; the Street playable occupant and shared zero-page workspace are active. Outputs: Stores $FF to $6C, $02B8, and $84; stores zero to $78, $02AF, $61, $63, $64, $66, $9F, $B3, $B6, $B4, $72, $F2, $7D, $BF, and $0279; stores $98 to $86; A returns $98. Clobbers: A, N, and Z plus the listed RAM state; X, Y, C, and V are preserved.

Sample and normalize gameplay input and process edge-triggered interface controls for The Street. Inputs: active-low control-port-2 state, control-port-1/keyboard state, keyboard-select table `$1DA5`, previous edge latches, and current interface state. Outputs: `$7C` bits 0–4 from control-port-2 direction/fire and bit 5 from the POTX threshold, raw keyboard rows `$0260-$0267`, edge latches `$02AA-$02AE/$02BF`, and phase interface/action state. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and scanner/interface scratch. Hardware: writes `$FF`, keyboard-row masks, and `$80` to CIA 1 port A `$DC00`; reads `$DC00`, CIA 1 port B `$DC01`, and SID POTX `$D419`; on the F1 edge that switches the music off (`$AA` flipped to zero) it clears SID registers `$D400-$D417`.

Text "MODE  ", drawn by the call at $90C1 that comes before it: column 17, row 20, colours $03 and $E6, then 6 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The second space, at $90CD, is a placeholder: the instruction at $90BE writes the mode $03F3 (0 to 2) plus $1C into it before the call, so the line reads MODE 1, MODE 2 or MODE 3. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $90CF.
Text 90c4 plus 9, the address the instruction at $90BE writes: byte 9 of the table at $90C4.
The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "MODE" at $90CE, and the routine that called it at $90C1 goes on.

Initial sequence byte zero and the current-value indexed base for the hidden-input recognizer at $9100. Together with the next-byte alias $911C it stores 19 values $911B-$912D; the scanner advances $BF only when normalized input matches the expected change. After the 18th matched change it sets $02AF=$FF, the request to end the level.
Expected next value of the 19-byte control sequence beginning at $911B, read with the current progress X at $9105. This is an overlapping indexed base, not another allocated array.

Apply the entrance rules for the exit the player arrived by and for the current area. Inputs: $0278, the exit record the player arrived by (an index into the tables at $8E69 on), and the current area $A2. Outputs: the entrance animation's kind and length from the list at $91BB go to $0293/$0294 (kind 0 when $0278 is not listed); exit $17 sets $74=$98 and $EF=$FF; in area $0D with item flag $03E9 set, the first collision coordinate is copied ($F8A4 to $F8A6) and it returns; otherwise InitializeRoomSpecificEntranceState installs the AI scripts and sprite colours of areas $0A, $0E, $0F, $10 and $11. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and AI-script state. Hardware: writes the sprite multicolour registers $D025/$D026 directly in areas $0A, $0E, $10 and $11.

The Street's own entrance rules, chosen by the area number in Y: area 3 draws object scene $BAB7 unless flag $03E9 is set, when it opens the wall instead (below); area 5 sets $F8 to 4 and starts animation $C6A5 in the second actor's slot; area 7 sets $F8 to 3 and starts $C6C4 there; areas 1, 4 and 8, the three with a car, set the two sprite multicolours $D025 and $D026 to 2 and 1, red and white; area 14 draws object scene $BAB0 when flag $03EB is set. Any other area returns.

OpenAreaThreeWall: copies the first wall's start X ($F8A4) into its end X ($F8A6), so that the first wall of area 3 ends where it begins and no longer stops the player, and returns with A zero. The entrance rules come here when flag $03E9 is set, and object record 0 calls it before its object is taken: the zero it returns lets the take go ahead, which sets $03E9 (item 17).

The Street's entrance-animation list, three bytes an entry as in Central Park's at $96A6 (the exit the player arrived by, the animation kind, how many animation steps it lasts), ending with $FF. This level's has no entries: only the $FF.

Mark all eight actor slots inactive and clear their key state bytes. Inputs: none. Outputs: $61, $63, and the corresponding $0210 and $0248 slot arrays are cleared. Clobbers: A is zero, Y exits as $FF, and flags change; X is preserved.

The address ApplySceneEntryRules reads the third byte of an entrance-animation entry from ($9144, with X stepping by three). With the list at $91BB empty the read never happens here; the address is the operand of ClearActorSlots's first instruction.

Copy the 1000-byte screen-color staging image into C64 color RAM. Inputs: staging bytes $0800-$0BE7 and visible C64 I/O. Outputs: color RAM $D800-$DBE7 receives the corresponding low nybbles; the last 24 cells of the third page are harmlessly copied twice. Clobbers: A, X, and flags; X returns zero. Hardware: writes color RAM $D800-$DBE7.

Provide The Street's reserved per-tick runtime hook. Inputs: A normal JSR return address on the stack. Outputs: Returns immediately without changing gameplay state. Clobbers: Registers and flags are preserved; RTS consumes the normal return address.

Provide The Street's reserved presentation-initialization hook. Inputs: A normal JSR return address on the stack. Outputs: Returns immediately without changing presentation state. Clobbers: Registers and flags are preserved; RTS consumes the normal return address.

RTS: where The Street's title load points PlayNextLoadVector at $3FF6. The one call through that vector, from StartLevelLoad (engine $1405), comes once as the game starts, before any level is loaded, and goes through the engine's own JMP $0E00 there, so this RTS is never reached.
RenderConditionalSceneVariant: The Street draws the plain scene of the current area ($A2) every time, with none of the variants Central Park chooses with its flags.

The two items the game expects the player to hold when leaving the level: item 1 and item 10. ResolveLevelCompletion reads them at $8BA6 with X counting to two and looks each up in the item flags at $03D8; with either missing it asks ARE YOU SURE YOU ARE PREPARED FOR THE NEXT LEVEL, and YES leaves the level all the same.

When the player's level-condition latch is active and no player animation script is running, force zero health and install the facing-specific terminal animation
Inputs: condition latch $B6, player animation-pointer high byte $61, and facing byte $69; animation streams begin at $BCB3 and $BCA7
Outputs: sets player health $0229=0 and tail-installs one of the two terminal animation streams; otherwise returns unchanged
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and the state changed by InstallAnimation

Hide the parts of an actor's sprites that are behind the current area's foreground pictures, then stage the sprites. Inputs: X is the first sprite slot to process (0 for the player, 4 for the other actor, or an auxiliary slot); it works up to slot 3, or slot 7 when X is 4 or more. A is the actor's depth ($74 or $74,X), compared with byte 1 of each 4-byte record in the area's list (pointers at $94CB, an $FF ends a list; a record is a picture's scene index, a depth, a column and a row). Outputs: for each drawn slot ($0218 bit 4 or 6 set, $0210 non-zero), every record whose depth is at least A is tested by TestSceneConditionRecord ($92CE): where the picture overlaps the 24-by-21 sprite, the sprite's pixel pairs under the picture's non-zero pixels are cleared and $0218 bit 4 is set. Then, with interrupts off, each slot with $0218 bit 6 gets its position, pointer ($30 or $38 plus the slot) and colour bits staged in $0240, $0258 and $0250, and $0210 is copied to $0248. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and masking scratch.

Mask one foreground picture out of a sprite slot. Inputs: ($ED) points at the area's list of 4-byte records (scene index, depth, column, row) and Y at the depth byte of one of them; $1F is the sprite slot, and $F4/$F6 and $F5 its X (low and high bytes) and Y. Outputs: the record's picture is placed at column x 8 and row x 8 + $1A, with the width and height from its header byte; if it does not overlap the 24-by-21 sprite the routine returns at once, otherwise it sets bit 4 of the slot's $0218 and clears, in the slot's sprite image, every pixel pair that lies under a non-zero pixel pair of the picture. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $04-$07, $1C/$1D, $21/$22, $25/$26, $8C/$8D, $D7-$DB and the slot's sprite image.

24 entries: eight zeroes, eight ones and eight twos. $93FC/$9412/$9428/$943E use clipped horizontal pixel X to select the destination byte within a three-byte sprite row. Paired with the clearing masks at $94B2; X advances two hires pixels per multicolor source pair.

24 entries: $3F,$3F,$CF,$CF,$F3,$F3,$FC,$FC repeated for three sprite bytes. The scene-condition renderer ANDs these into the selected sprite-row byte whenever the corresponding source pixel pair is nonzero. This removes a two-bit pair, selected jointly with the byte-offset lookup at $949A. Ends at $94C9; $94CA is a zero byte between it and the pointer directory, which no instruction reads.

ServiceEnemyBoundaryLatch, The Street's version: when $F8 is 3 or 4 (set on entering area 7 or area 5) and the second actor's animation has finished ($63 is zero), it keeps only bit 0 of the command flags $81 and, if that bit was set, starts animation $C6CB (for 3) or $C6AC (for 4) in the second actor's slot. The bit is set when the player walks into one of the walls in those areas that carry command 40 (area 7) or 39 (area 5): SegmentCollision adds one to $81 for the touch ($B48E). The two animations carry events 20 and 19, which hurt the player standing at a fixed spot.

AdvanceCrossingLights, called from MainTick every pass: once $B0 reaches 50 it resets it to zero, flips the light state $03EA between 0 and $FF and draws the current area's light. $B0 counts every fourth 50 Hz interrupt tick, so the lights change every four seconds.

DrawCrossingLight: looks the current area up in the light table at $9A78 (sorted by area, so it stops at the first larger one) and draws the light scene the table gives for the present state of $03EA. EnterArea also calls it after drawing a new area, so the light is right as soon as the player arrives.
the light state, compared with the entry's red state
not red: the second scene, two bytes on

The crossing lights, six bytes an entry, sorted by area and ending with $FF: the area, the light state in which it shows red, the scene drawn when $03EA equals that state (the red light) and the scene drawn when it does not (the green). Area 1, red on 0: $BAC7, $BACC. Area 4, red on 0: $BAD1, $BAD6. Area 5, red on $FF: $BADB, $BAE0. Area 8, red on 0: $BAE5, $BAEA. Area 9, red on 0: $BAEF, $BAF4. Area 11, red on 0: $BAF9, $BAFE.
The light table plus 1, read at $9A64 with X at an entry's start: the light state in which that crossing shows red, compared with $03EA.
The light table plus 2, read at $9A6B: the low byte of the scene to draw, at X+2 for the red light or, once X has been moved on by two, X+4 for the green.
The light table plus 3, read at $9A70: the high byte of the scene to draw, at X+3 for the red light or X+5 for the green.

Advance the scripted animation attached to a boundary event. Inputs: actor activity $61, sequence state $0293, and countdown $0294. Outputs: the timer and state advance and the selected animation may be installed. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and animation state.

Conditionally dispatch the pending script command through the Street target-minus-one table
Inputs: command/state bytes $80/$81 and player animation-pointer high byte $61; $80 low six bits select the command; the target-minus-one words start at $9B31 and are read from the base $9B2F with X = twice the command
Outputs: when $81 is negative and the bit-6/$61 gate admits it, transfers to the selected command handler by RTS dispatch; command zero or a failed gate returns normally
Clobbers: A, X, flags and two stack bytes before dispatch; Y is preserved until the selected handler

RTS completing the stack-built dispatch at $9B28. The high-byte indexed load uses this address as its base with X=2*command, so nonzero commands read the high bytes of target-minus-one words beginning at $9B31. This byte is executable RTS, not the start of a standalone pointer array. Command zero returns before dispatch.

46 words, each the routine for one script command, from command 1 up less one: the dispatcher pushes it and returns into it. Targets: $9B8D, $9B91, $9B95, $9B99, $9BBC, $9BBC, $9C04, $9C00, $9BF6, $9BBC, $9CF6, $9BBB, $9C3F, $9C50, $9C60, $9CF0, $9C3B, $9C37, $9C23, $9C64, $9C0E, $9BBC, $9C2F, $9CFA, $9C2B, $9C27, $9C1B, $9D04, $9BBB, $9CEA, $9CE3, $9D08, $9D0C, $9D10, $9D1A, $9D34, $9D4E, $9D68, $9D8E, $9D8E, $9D8F, $9BBC, $9BF6, $9BBC, $9BF6, $9BF6.

Return at once, for the script commands that have no action. Its RTS returns to the code that called ScriptDispatch: the address the dispatcher pushed was used up by the RTS at $9B30 that jumped here. Inputs and outputs: none. Clobbers: nothing.

Run the heading-7, state-$70-zero scripted animation sequence, then consume the pending command.
Inputs: Current heading $69, state $70, command $81, and animation data beginning at $BD33/$BD38/$BD4D.
Outputs: On heading 7 with $70 zero, runs one $BD33 animation, two $BD38 animations, then $BD4D, sets $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to $98 and $EF to $FF, which holds it there, and calls resident pacing $11F1; always clears $81 before returning.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $EF, $81, animation/actor state, and pacing scratch.

Set $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to $9E and hold it there ($EF = $FF stops ApplySignedActorHeightDelta changing it), then run the common eight-cycle fatal sequence.
Inputs: Current animation/actor state.
Outputs: Stores $74=$9E and $EF=$FF, then runs eight cycles and sets death latch $B6=$FF.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $EF, $0234, animation/actor scratch, and $B6.

Copy the player's Y ($55) into $74, the Y the scene conditions test, and run the common eight-cycle fatal sequence.
Inputs: Player Y $55 (its whole-pixel byte; $51 holds the fraction) and current animation/actor state.
Outputs: Stores $55 into $74, then runs eight cycles and sets death latch $B6=$FF.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $0234, animation/actor scratch, and $B6.

Advance eight scripted animation/update cycles and latch player death.
Inputs: $74 and $EF as the script left them, and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Calls $9CB7 with A=8, which marks $0234 and advances eight cycles, then writes $B6=$FF.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $0234, animation/actor scratch, and $B6.

When command bit 0 is set, set $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to 0, run two scripted animation/update cycles and then ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($9CFA), which takes two points of the player's energy; then consume the command.
Inputs: Command flags $81 and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Armed path stores $74=0 and enters the two-cycle entry at $9C3B, whose tail calls ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($9CFA) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which it does not read: it takes two points of the player's energy $0229 through DamagePlayer; both paths clear $81 before return.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $81, $0229, $0234, and animation/actor scratch; when the energy runs out, also $6D and the death latch $B6.

Set $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to $5D, hold it there with $EF = $FF, advance one scripted animation/update cycle and run ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($9CFA), which takes two points of the player's energy.
Inputs: Current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Stores $74=$5D and $EF=$FF, calls the one-cycle path through $9CB7, then ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($9CFA) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which it does not read: it takes two points of the player's energy $0229 through DamagePlayer, then clears command $81.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $EF, $81, $0229, $0234, and animation/actor scratch; when the energy runs out, also $6D and the death latch $B6.

Advance 1 scripted animation/update cycle and run ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($9CFA), which takes two points of the player's energy, then consume the pending command.
Inputs: $74 and $EF as the script left them, and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Calls $9CB7 with A=1; after the bounded loop, calls ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($9CFA) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which it does not read: it takes two points of the player's energy $0229 through DamagePlayer, then clears $81 and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $81, $0229, $0234, and animation/actor scratch; when the energy runs out, also $6D and the death latch $B6.

Command $1A loads $5D, then branches to $9C31 to store it in $74, the Y the scene conditions test, set $EF=$FF and run one scripted update cycle and then ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($9CFA) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which it does not read: it takes two points of the player's energy $0229 through DamagePlayer, before clearing command $81. This entry shares that tail with the $00 and $7D variants; it differs from $9C1B in its branch path.

Set $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to $00, hold it there with $EF = $FF, advance one scripted animation/update cycle and run ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($9CFA), which takes two points of the player's energy.
Inputs: Current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Stores $74=$00 and $EF=$FF, calls the one-cycle path through $9CB7, then ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($9CFA) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which it does not read: it takes two points of the player's energy $0229 through DamagePlayer, then clears command $81.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $EF, $81, $0229, $0234, and animation/actor scratch; when the energy runs out, also $6D and the death latch $B6.

Set $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to $7D, hold it there with $EF = $FF, advance one scripted animation/update cycle and run ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($9CFA), which takes two points of the player's energy.
Inputs: Current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Stores $74=$7D and $EF=$FF, calls the one-cycle path through $9CB7, then ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($9CFA) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which it does not read: it takes two points of the player's energy $0229 through DamagePlayer, then clears command $81.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $EF, $81, $0229, $0234, and animation/actor scratch; when the energy runs out, also $6D and the death latch $B6.

Command $12 loads A=1 and branches to the bounded update loop at $9C41. $74 and $EF stay as the script left them; the tail calls $9CB7 once, then ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($9CFA) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which it does not read: it takes two points of the player's energy $0229 through DamagePlayer, and clears $81. Unlike the target-setting entries, this entry writes neither $74 nor $EF itself.

Advance 2 scripted animation/update cycles and run ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($9CFA), which takes two points of the player's energy, then consume the pending command.
Inputs: $74 and $EF as the script left them, and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Calls $9CB7 with A=2; after the bounded loop, calls ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($9CFA) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which it does not read: it takes two points of the player's energy $0229 through DamagePlayer, then clears $81 and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $81, $0229, $0234, and animation/actor scratch; when the energy runs out, also $6D and the death latch $B6.

Script command 13: plays the player's facing animation four times through, running the engine until each one ends (RepeatScriptRuntimeFrames, A = 4), then, where Central Park runs its scripted coordinate sequence with X = $F8 and Y = 4, calls ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand at $9CFA, so the player loses two points of energy. It clears the command $81 and returns. The Street has no copy of that sequence; every call that went to it goes to $9CFA here. No wall in The Street carries command 13, and the walls are the only source of commands, so it never runs in this level.

When command bit 0 is set, run seven scripted cycles and enter the common death-latch tail; otherwise only clear the command.
Inputs: Command flags $81 and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Armed path calls $9CB7 with A=7 then writes $B6=$FF; unarmed path clears $81 without damage.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $81, $0234, animation/actor scratch, and on the armed path $B6.

When command bit 0 is set, set $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to $04, hold it there with $EF = $FF, run seven cycles, and latch death.
Inputs: Command flags $81 and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Armed path stores $74=$04/$EF=$FF and enters the seven-cycle fatal tail; unarmed path clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $EF, $81, $0234, animation/actor scratch, and on the armed path $B6.

When command bit 0 is set, set $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to $0C, hold it there with $EF = $FF, run seven cycles, and latch death.
Inputs: Command flags $81 and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Armed path stores $74=$0C/$EF=$FF and enters the seven-cycle fatal tail; unarmed path clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $EF, $81, $0234, animation/actor scratch, and on the armed path $B6.

Run The Street's fixed animation at $BD7E the requested number of times, run the finishing animation at $BD93 once, then synchronize three engine-tick stamps. Inputs: A is a nonzero repetition count; animation streams $BD7E and $BD93, actor state, the blocking runtime loop, and resident tick-snapshot helper $11F1 are active. Outputs: Each $BD7E cycle is installed and serviced until $61 clears; $BD93 is then installed and serviced once; finally $026C, $026E, and $0277 receive the current engine tick $E2 and A returns that tick. Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, transient stack contents, animation/runtime state, and $026C/$026E/$0277. Hardware: Through the blocking runtime loop, advances sprite/display state and reads controls; this wrapper and the $11F1 timer-snapshot tail perform no direct I/O.

Install an animation and run the blocking script runtime loop. Inputs: A:X is the animation pointer and the actor context is valid. Outputs: the animation is installed and the runtime loop completes. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and runtime state. Hardware: changes sprite presentation indirectly through the engine.

Run script-time engine frames until the active actor or action completes. Inputs: an installed animation and valid runtime state. Outputs: enemy AI, auxiliary sprites, input, and animation state advance until $61 clears. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and broad frame scratch. Hardware: changes sprite and display state indirectly and reads input through the called joystick poller.

Advance the player's and then the enemy's animation by one eligible engine step, at most once a tick. Inputs: tick $E2 and timer slot 2 ($026A, interval 1 at $9E4D); both actors' animation state. Outputs: when no tick has passed since the last call the gate at $9E37 returns straight to RunScriptRuntimeLoop; otherwise AnimationInterpreter ($A16F, X=0) steps the player's animation, and ScheduleEnemyAnimation ($A15A) steps the enemy's when its own tick has advanced. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and animation scratch.

Execute a scripted action for a fixed number of completed animation cycles. Inputs: A is the repetition count and actor facing and animation state are valid. Outputs: the count is exhausted and scripted state advances. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, stack, and $0234. Hardware: changes sprite and display state indirectly.

Install one of two player-animation descriptors selected from the current facing direction. Inputs: Player facing $69 and Street animation descriptors $C693 and $C69C. Outputs: A:X contains the selected descriptor and control tail-transfers to InstallAnimation, which initializes $60/$61, $5C, $58, $96, and $5D. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and animation state through the tail-called installer.

Script command 31. Where Central Park tests its clearance predicate here and then runs its scripted coordinate sequence, The Street calls ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand at $9CFA instead. That returns with A zero, so this always goes on to $9CF0, which sets X to $07 and Y to 2 (values only the missing sequence would have read) and goes on into the same routine again: the player loses two points of energy twice and the command is cleared. No wall in The Street carries command 31, and the walls are the only source of commands, so it never runs in this level.

Script command 30. Where Central Park tests its clearance predicate here and then runs its scripted coordinate sequence, The Street calls ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand at $9CFA instead. That returns with A zero, so this always goes on to $9CF6, which sets X to $0E and Y to 0 (values only the missing sequence would have read) and goes on into the same routine again: the player loses two points of energy twice and the command is cleared. No wall in The Street carries command 30, and the walls are the only source of commands, so it never runs in this level.

Sets X to $07 and Y to 2 and goes on to ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand at $9CFA, which ignores them: Central Park's scripted coordinate sequence, which would have read them, is not in this level.

Sets X to $0E and Y to 0 and goes on to ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand at $9CFA, which ignores them: Central Park's scripted coordinate sequence, which would have read them, is not in this level.

Apply two units of player damage and consume the pending script command.
Inputs: Player energy $0229 and command $81.
Outputs: Calls DamagePlayer with A=2, then clears $81.
Clobbers: A, flags, $0229 and $81; when the energy runs out, also $6D and the death latch $B6.

Request enemy projectile type 2 through the fixed second projectile slot and consume the pending command.
Inputs: Enemy position/heading $56/$57/$6B, projectile slot 1 state $0281/$0283/$0285/$0287/$0289, and command $81.
Outputs: Passes A=2 to $B012; if slot 1 is free and the derived coordinate is in range it initializes the slot, then clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, projectile slot-1 fields, $0296, and $81.

Request enemy projectile type 3 through the fixed second projectile slot and consume the pending command.
Inputs: Enemy position/heading $56/$57/$6B, projectile slot 1 state $0281/$0283/$0285/$0287/$0289, and command $81.
Outputs: Passes A=3 to $B012; if slot 1 is free and the derived coordinate is in range it initializes the slot, then clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, projectile slot-1 fields, $0296, and $81.

Request enemy projectile type 4 through the fixed second projectile slot and consume the pending command.
Inputs: Enemy position/heading $56/$57/$6B, projectile slot 1 state $0281/$0283/$0285/$0287/$0289, and command $81.
Outputs: Passes A=4 to $B012; if slot 1 is free and the derived coordinate is in range it initializes the slot, then clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, projectile slot-1 fields, $0296, and $81.

Request enemy projectile type 5 through the fixed second projectile slot and consume the pending command.
Inputs: Enemy position/heading $56/$57/$6B, projectile slot 1 state $0281/$0283/$0285/$0287/$0289, and command $81.
Outputs: Passes A=5 to $B012; if slot 1 is free and the derived coordinate is in range it initializes the slot, then clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, projectile slot-1 fields, $0296, and $81.

Script command 35, set by a wall in the road of area 1 (its command byte is 99, command 35 with bit 6 set): if the light state $03EA is 0, when area 1's light shows red, and the second actor's Y position $57 is zero, it starts the car's animation $C7BD in the second actor's slot and takes $2C from the player's energy. It clears the command either way.
the second actor's Y position

Script command 36, set by a wall in the road of area 4 (command byte 100): if the light state $03EA is not zero, when area 4's light shows green, and $57 is zero, it starts the car's animation $C7DB in the second actor's slot and takes $2C from the player's energy. It clears the command either way.

Script command 37, set by a wall in the road of area 8 (command byte 101): if $03EA is 0, when area 8's light shows red, and $57 is zero, it starts the car's animation $C7E7 in the second actor's slot and takes $2C from the player's energy. It clears the command either way.

Script command 38, set by four walls in area 14 (command byte 38): once flag $03EB is set (item 19, taken in area 14 with item 11 selected) and bit 0 of $81 is set, it clears $74 and moves the player down two pixels at a time, 16 times, composing the picture and testing the scene conditions after each step, then leaves the area by transition variant 2.

RTS: script commands 39 and 40, which walls in areas 5 and 7 carry, do nothing themselves in The Street; the touch that sets them also adds one to $81 and sets its bit 7 (SegmentCollision, $B48E), and ServiceEnemyBoundaryLatch at $9A05 acts on bit 0 of $81.

Advance the player actor for the elapsed IRQ ticks, selecting control, script, animation, movement, collision, and logical-sprite work
Inputs: tick $E2/$026C, timed-event state $0293, player script pointer $60/$61, movement/action state $50/$51,$54/$55,$5C,$65,$68/$69,$70,$79,$89, and normalized input $7C
Outputs: stamps elapsed delta in $8F and $026C; advances timed events or control/script state; updates player coordinates, motion/pose/action, collision state, and logical sprite component buffers
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and player-driver, movement, collision, animation, and sprite-composition scratch

Compose the player's image and hide the parts behind the area's foreground pictures. Inputs: desired direction $68 (its bit from $1DA5 goes to $1E), facing $69, frame $65, depth $74 and the current area's foreground list. Outputs: logical sprite slots 0-3 hold frame $65, mirrored for facing indexes 1 and 3 (the flags at $A38E); ComposeSprites clears $9F; MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery clears the sprite pixels behind the foreground pictures and stages the slots in $0240-$025F. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E, and compositor and masking scratch. Hardware: changes sprite or image RAM; no VIC-II register is written directly.

Compose the Street playable phase's player frame $65 into logical actor slot 0, mirrored when the facing flag at $A38E,X ANDed with $1E is non-zero.
Inputs: X is the facing index ($69 shifted right once) into the four mirror flags at $A38E; $1E is the direction bit of $68; $65 is the frame; player position/facing and sprite work buffers are current.
Outputs: Passes $A38E,X AND $1E to ComposeSprites as the mirror flag, with X=0 and Y=$65, composes logical actor slot 0, then falls through to $9E30, which masks the player's sprites behind the area's foreground pictures.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, sprite-composition scratch/buffers, and masking scratch.
Hardware: No direct VIC-II register write; the composition helper updates sprite work buffers and changes $01 transiently before restoring it.

Mask the Street playable phase's player sprites, actor slot 0, against the area's foreground pictures without recomposing its frame.
Inputs: Player sprite slots 0-3 are composed; $74 supplies the vertical coordinate compared with each foreground record's depth byte; the area's foreground list (pointers at $94CB) is current.
Outputs: Sets X=0, loads A=$74, and tail-enters MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery ($9217), which clears the sprite pixels behind the foreground pictures and stages the slots' positions, pointers and colours in $0240-$025F.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, and masking scratch; the slots' positions are read from $0200/$0208/$0210.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Rate-limit an update and abort its caller when the slot's minimum interval has not passed. Inputs: X timer slot (2 for the script loop's animation step, 5 for DrawActiveObject, 9 and 10 for the two auxiliary sprite slots, 12 for OpponentAI), global tick $E2, per-slot stamp $0268,X, and threshold table $9E4B. Outputs: the eligible path updates timing state; the ineligible path returns to the caller's caller. Clobbers: A, flags, timing state, and two stack bytes on the abort path.

16 slot-indexed minimum intervals. $9E3A subtracts the slot's last tick $0268,X from current $E2, $9E3D compares the difference to this table and the gate discards the caller return frame when too soon; accepted calls update the saved tick. Most intervals are 1, with exceptions 6,2 and4 in the captured table; the slots this level uses are 2, 5, 9, 10 and 12, so the 2 at slot 7 is not read.

Translate the normalized Street input byte and current player state into facing, movement, pose, action, and animation requests
Inputs: normalized active-high control byte $7C (a set bit is a pressed direction or fire); death/condition latch $B6; player state $61,$65,$68/$69,$6C/$6D,$70,$89; decode tables at $A009 and $9FA5
Outputs: updates desired direction $68, facing $69, action/motion $6C/$6D, pose $65, dirty flag $9F, and may select/install a player animation
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and player-control/animation scratch

Continuation of $9E5B control interpretation: applies desired heading $68, allowing odd headings to replace $69 except an exact opposite; marks redraw $9F when changed. Sets movement $6C and derives facing/pose $65 and $6D. The $9ED4 idle path clears $02B8 and may select an idle animation; $9EFE onward handles changes in the fire/action state $78, comparing direction to facing before selecting an action through $9F6D. Uses $9FA5 and $A009 direction lookups; no direct hardware writes. Entry is within the larger control routine, not an independent callable API.

Translate action code A into the Street playable phase's player animation pointer and install that animation.
Inputs: A is the action code selected by the control logic (InterpretControls and InterpretNormalizedControls); $69 is player facing; phase animation lookup tables are valid.
Outputs: Stores A in $60, derives the facing-adjusted animation index, loads its pointer, initializes $60/$61/$5C/$58/$96/$5D, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $58, $5C/$5D, $60/$61, $6D, and $96.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Install a new player animation-bytecode stream and prime its first control byte
Inputs: X = stream low byte; A = stream high byte; desired direction $68 and facing $69
Outputs: stores the stream pointer in $60/$61, loads its first byte into $5C, clears animation delay $58, copies $68 to $96, and stores $69 bit 1 in $5D
Clobbers: A, Y, and flags; X is preserved

Eight action-heading values 1,7,1,7,5,3,5,3 selected at $9F5B. Index combines desired cardinal direction and current facing, then output replaces desired heading $68 before action animation selection. This is separate from the joystick low-nibble map $A009.

Interpret the Street playable phase's normalized control latch and update player motion/action animation state.
Inputs: $7C is the control byte normalized by ScanAndNormalizeInput ($8F5D); player animation, action, timing, facing, and collision state are current.
Outputs: Maps the low control nybble through the direction table at $A009; a new direction, or none, restarts the hold timer $85, sets $88=$FF and sets $6D to the facing halved; once the same direction has been held for the delay from $A001 (4 or 8 ticks) it selects action $84 x 4 + 8 (plus $20 when $70 is 0 or 4 and up) through SelectPlayerAnimationForAction, and again at once while the player's mode class is $10. The facing $69 is read, not written.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, player input/action/timing fields ($84, $85, $88, $6D), and animation-installation state on paths that select a new animation.
Hardware: No direct CIA or other hardware-register writes.

Eight alternating delays 4,8 indexed by normalized direction Y. $9FDA compares elapsed tick difference against the chosen threshold before deriving action code $84*4+8, plus $20 when $70 is 0 or 4 and up, and selecting animation. This table controls action timing, not the joystick direction conversion.

16-entry map of the low four normalized control bits to eight directions 0..7 or $FF for no valid direction. $9E74, $9F22 and $9FB2 use it to choose movement/facing/action; opposing direction combinations map to $FF. Fire occupies a different input bit and is handled separately.

36 words, each one of the player's animations. Targets: $BBB4, $BBC7, $BBDC, $BBEE, $BC3A, $BC4B, $BBA0, $BBAA, $BC89, $BC99, $BD21, $BD0F, $BC00, $BC0D, $BD21, $BD0F, $BC59, $BC71, $BBA0, $BBAA, $BC1B, $BC29, $BBA0, $BBAA, $BC3A, $BC4B, $BD21, $BD0F, $BC00, $BC0D, $BD21, $BD0F, $BC3A, $BC4B, $BBA0, $BBAA.
PlayerAnimationPointers plus 1, the address the instruction at $9F89 reads with Y as the index: the high byte of each word of the table, the index counting in pairs from the low byte.

18 action-mode bases used at $9F76: the action code A shifted right twice picks one, and the facing $69 shifted right once is added to it to give the player's action mode $6D, the value the control and combat code compares (as $6D with its low two bits masked) with $10, $0C and $24. The animation pointer at $A019 is chosen separately, from A itself plus 0 or 2 for the facing. Values include $0C,$04,$18,$10,$1C,$14,$20,$28.

Build, advance, validate, and commit the player's movement candidate for this tick
Inputs: player position $54/$55 and its fractional bytes $50/$51; enemy position $56/$57; desired direction $68; facing $69; elapsed steps $8F; direction-mask table $1DA5
Outputs: initializes candidate $48-$4D and opposing position $C9/$CA, calls AdvanceCandidate, commits candidate position and fractions back to $54/$55,$50/$51, and reports vertical displacement through the shared tail at $A136 with X=0
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and candidate/collision scratch including $1E,$48-$4D,$C9/$CA

Build and advance the enemy movement candidate, record collision outcomes, and commit it only inside the playable bounds
Inputs: enemy position $56/$57 and its fractional bytes $52/$53; player position $54/$55; desired direction $6A; facing $6B; elapsed steps $8F; profile selector $D3; direction-mask table $1DA5
Outputs: updates candidate/collision scratch; records collision in $02B0/$02B2/$02B4 or failure count $02B1; commits $56/$57,$52/$53 only for X in [$02,$F6] and Y in [$09,$BC]; reports vertical displacement through $A136 with X=2
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and candidate/collision scratch including $1E,$48-$4D,$C9/$CA,$CD

Add the signed number in A to the actor's $74,X, unless $EF is set or $74,X is 0 or $FF. A positive sum is held at $FF; a negative one is not held at zero but wraps, since the BCS at $A155 goes on to the next instruction either way. Inputs: A, and X the actor's offset. Outputs: $74,X. Clobbers: A and flags; X and Y are kept.

Run the enemy animation interpreter once when the IRQ tick has advanced
Inputs: current tick $E2, enemy animation stamp $026E, and the already-installed enemy animation stream/state at actor offset 2
Outputs: if no tick elapsed, returns unchanged; otherwise stores elapsed delta in $8F, stamps $026E, sets X=2, and tail-enters the shared animation interpreter
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $8F, $026E, and all animation-interpreter scratch/state on the admitted path

Interpret one elapsed step of the selected actor's animation bytecode, including delay, pose, coordinate deltas, event generation, and continuation
Inputs: X=0 at $A16F for player or X=2 at $A171 for enemy; pointer $60/$61,X; control/delay $5C/$58-$59,X; actor position $54/$55,X; elapsed ticks $8F
Outputs: advances delay and stream position, updates pose $65,X, position $54/$55,X, event $64,X, continuation pointer, movement flags, and recomposes the actor's logical sprites when required
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and animation, movement, event, collision, and sprite-composition scratch

Run the Street playable phase's animation interpreter for the scheduled enemy slot.
Inputs: X is the enemy animation-state offset selected by the scheduler (normally 2); $61,X is its stream pointer high byte; timing and animation state are current.
Outputs: Honors animation delay, decodes one bytecode step when due, updates the enemy animation/movement/event state, composes the resulting actor frame when requested, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02/$03, animation timing/pointer/state bytes for slot X, actor-frame/sprite scratch, and event state selected by the bytecode.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes; bytecode paths requesting composition alter sprite work buffers and change CPU-port banking transiently before restoring it.

Compose an actor's current frame and hide the parts behind the area's foreground pictures. Inputs: X and $4F the actor offset (0 player, 2 enemy) and current animation frame $65,X; the mirror flag is $5D,X when $5C,X bit 4 is set, else $5C,X bit 6; depth $74,X. Outputs: the player is composed into sprite slots 0-3 with ComposeSprites, the enemy into slots 4-7 with ComposeEnemySprites; MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery then clears the sprite pixels behind the foreground pictures and stages the slots in $0240-$025F. X is not restored: it returns as 4 for the player and 8 for the enemy. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and shared renderer scratch. Hardware: it writes no chip register itself; the composer it calls switches the I/O area out through the processor port $01 while it reads the packed sprites and puts it back, and MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery stages the slots with interrupts off and ends with CLI.

Return immediately from the Street playable phase's animation interpreter on the shared no-further-work path.
Inputs: The preceding animation branch has completed or determined that no frame composition is needed.
Outputs: Returns to the interpreter's caller without additional state or hardware changes.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and memory are preserved; RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.
Delay for the requested number of engine ticks. Inputs: A is the tick count. Outputs: the requested tick transitions have elapsed. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and wait scratch.

Advance an actor candidate by up to eight elapsed substeps and test each proposed segment against compiled collision geometry
Inputs: X = the mover's facing index ($69 or $6B shifted right once, 0-3); Y = movement-profile selector; old/candidate position $48-$4B; candidate fractional bytes $4C/$4D; direction mask $1E; elapsed count $8F
Outputs: stores profile in $027F and capped count in $8E; updates candidate coordinates; returns collision and trigger state through $23/$24,$80/$81,$CD and related movement scratch
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and broad candidate/collision scratch

Four negative-X masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $A279 in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask, the profile's X step ($11DD,Y low, $11E7,Y high) is subtracted from the candidate X, held at 0. Values $70,$C1,$70,$C1.

Four positive-X masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $A293 in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask, the profile's X step ($11DD,Y low, $11E7,Y high) is added to the candidate X, held at $FE. Values $07,$1C,$07,$1C.

Four negative-Y masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $A2AD in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask, and the horizontal guard at $A386 does not match, the profile's Y step ($11E2,Y low, $11EC,Y high) is subtracted from the candidate Y. Values $07,$C1,$07,$C1.

Four positive-Y masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $A2E9 in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask, and the horizontal guard at $A386 does not match, the profile's Y step ($11E2,Y low, $11EC,Y high) is added to the candidate Y. Values $70,$1C,$70,$1C.

Four vertical guard masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $A2CA and $A306 in AdvanceCandidate after a Y step. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask the same Y step is applied twice more, three times in all. All four are $11, directions 0 and 4.

Four horizontal guard masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $A2B4 and $A2F0 in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask the Y step is skipped. All four are $44, directions 2 and 6.

Four walk-cycle masks, one per facing index (the player's facing $69 shifted right once), read at $9DF9 in PlayerDriver. Each holds the three directions around that facing: $07 directions 0-2, $1C 2-4, $70 4-6, $C1 6, 7 and 0. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask the walk frame (the low three bits of $65) steps forward by one, otherwise back by one.

Four mirror flags, one per facing index (the player's facing $69 shifted right once), read at $9E24. The flag, ANDed with the direction bit in $1E, is passed to ComposeSprites as its mirror flag $F1, so facing indexes 1 and 3 draw the frame mirrored. Values $00,$FF,$00,$FF.

Consume and dispatch pending player and enemy animation events through the shared target-minus-one event table
Inputs: player event $64 and enemy event $66; event table begins at $A3B8; X=0 selects player and X=2 enemy
Outputs: dispatches each nonzero event through the RTS table, clears $64 after the player handler and $66 after the enemy handler, and returns after both channels are empty
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, two stack bytes per dispatch, and handler-dependent state

Dispatch an event handler through a target-minus-one RTS table. Inputs: A is the event index. Outputs: control transfers to the selected handler, which returns to the original caller. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, and two transient stack bytes.

24 words, each the routine for one animation event, from event 0 up less one: the dispatcher pushes it and returns into it. Targets: $A3E8, $A421, $A671, $A426, $A441, $A446, $AFBC, $A44B, $A450, $B89A, $B89F, $B8A4, $A421, $A43C, $A45B, $A3E9, $A441, $A41F, $A41B, $A3E9, $A3EF, $A3E9, $9B91, $A3E9.
EventDispatchTable plus 1, the address the instruction at $A3AF reads with Y as the index: the high byte of each word of the table, the index counting in pairs from the low byte.
RTS: the table's entry for event 0, which does nothing. No other event points here, and EventDispatch never dispatches event 0, since it skips a zero $64 or $66.
Events 15, 19, 21 and 23: a hazard at X 124, Y 115. The player loses $2C energy if they are less than 11 to either side of it and less than 7 above or below.
Event 20: the same hazard test as $A3E9, at X 219, Y 143.
near enough across?
near enough up or down?
DistanceFromPlayer: returns in X the distance between X and the player's X ($54), and in Y the distance between Y and the player's Y ($55), both without sign.
Event 18: loads X with $FC and branches into EventCopyState89To70, which copies $89 to $70 and never reads X.
Event 17: loads X with 4 and goes on into EventCopyState89To70, which copies $89 to $70 and never reads X.

Copy state byte $89 into actor-state byte $70 for two event codes.
Inputs: $89.
Outputs: Writes $70=$89 and returns with A equal to the copied value.
Clobbers: A and flags; $70.

Handle event 3 differently for the player channel and opponent channel.
Inputs: Actor selector X from event dispatch and current animation/AI state.
Outputs: For X=0, waits 20 engine ticks through WaitEngineTicks ($A25E, A=$14), resets the tick baselines through $11F1, and sets $B4=$FF; for X!=0, sets opponent AI state $CF=$0B.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, animation/pacing scratch, and either $B4 or $CF.

Apply $2C units of player damage for event $0D.
Inputs: Player energy $0229 and existing death state.
Outputs: Tail-calls DamagePlayer with A=$2C.
Clobbers: A, flags, player energy $0229, death latch $B6, and combat scratch.

Run object mode 3 for the player, then test the combat overlap and apply the actor-to-actor hit, damage, score, and reaction result
Inputs: X = attacking actor offset (0 player, 2 enemy); this entry sets Y=3, which ObjectEngine takes as its object mode when X is 0 (TestActorCombatOverlap then overwrites Y); actor geometry/state; action modes $6D/$6F; damage tables $A491/$A4A5
Outputs: on overlap, ignores a target already in reaction $24, otherwise selects damage, calls DamagePlayer or DamageEnemy, awards score through $1187 when the player is the attacker, and latches the opposing actor's reaction
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, overlap/damage/score scratch, and object-engine state on the player channel

Resolve the selected combat-contact event. Inputs: actor state and the contact type selected by the entry path. Outputs: damage, reaction animation, collision, and object state are updated. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and combat scratch. Hardware: may change presentation or audio indirectly through damage and animation helpers.

Run object mode 5 for the player, then resolve actor overlap and dispatch the resulting player/enemy damage and reaction.
Inputs: Actor selector X (the attacker), both actors' positions/headings/animation modes, energy fields, and collision profile tables $A631-$A670.
Outputs: Loads Y=5, which ObjectEngine takes as its object mode when X is 0 (the overlap test then overwrites Y); runs the shared overlap query, whose combat index comes from the attacker's mode $6D,X and state $70,X; on a hit applies damage to the opposing actor plus the corresponding reaction animation.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F/$C5/$C6, actor animation/combat state, energy, object-engine state, and possible death/defeat persistence.

Run object mode 6 for the player, then resolve actor overlap and dispatch the resulting player/enemy damage and reaction.
Inputs: Actor selector X (the attacker), both actors' positions/headings/animation modes, energy fields, and collision profile tables $A631-$A670.
Outputs: Loads Y=6, which ObjectEngine takes as its object mode when X is 0 (the overlap test then overwrites Y); runs the shared overlap query, whose combat index comes from the attacker's mode $6D,X and state $70,X; on a hit applies damage to the opposing actor plus the corresponding reaction animation.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F/$C5/$C6, actor animation/combat state, energy, object-engine state, and possible death/defeat persistence.

Resolve the Street playable phase's combat overlap for attacking actor slot X, selecting the player or opponent damage and reaction path.
Inputs: X selects the attacker, actor slot 0 or the opponent slot 2; Y is the object mode for ObjectEngine; actor positions and combat state are current.
Outputs: When X is 0, runs ObjectEngine ($B8A6) with Y as the object mode and sets X=0 again; then runs the overlap test itself at $A45B (TestActorCombatOverlap) and, on a hit, applies the matching hit/reaction/damage logic and updates actor/combat state. It returns no meaningful result.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, combat/reaction scratch, object-engine state, and the affected actor's health/action state.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Resolve combat overlap using the profile derived from the selected actor's current mode, then dispatch damage and reaction.
Inputs: Actor selector X plus both actors' positions, headings, animation modes, energies, and collision profile tables.
Outputs: Runs $A565 to derive the active profile and overlap result; on a hit applies actor-specific damage and reaction animation.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F/$C5/$C6, actor animation/combat state, energy, and possible death/defeat persistence.

20 attack strengths read at $A473 for an enemy attack against the player; each is the energy DamagePlayer subtracts. Index $1F is the enemy's attack mode $6F minus $14 shifted right twice (0-3, since its attack modes are $14-$23), ORed with its profile $72 times 4 (a profile of 4 and up counts as 0), so only entries 0-15 can be read; the result enters the saturating player-damage routine $AE35. The last four bytes ($A4A1-$A4A4) are not reached by this index.

16 attack values read at $A47C/$A482 for player attacks, passed both to score accounting $1187 and the enemy-damage routine DamageEnemy ($AE53). That routine subtracts the value from the enemy's energy $022A, held at 0: it is conventional energy subtraction, and the IRQ only moves the displayed meter $022B,X toward the energy.

Select and install the victim's hit-reaction animation. Inputs: X the victim's offset (0 player, 2 enemy); the victim's facing $69,X, mode $6D,X and energy, and the attacker's mode. Outputs: unless the victim's mode class is already $24, $6D,X is saved in $71,X and set to the facing halved plus $24. If the victim still has energy, a reaction pointer from the table at $A525, chosen by the attacker's mode and the victim's facing, is installed: for the player through InstallAnimation, with $02BD cleared, and for the enemy through InstallAiScript. If the victim's energy is 0, the player gets no new animation and $02BD is cleared, and the enemy gets the defeat script $BCB3 or $BCA7 (by $6B bit 2) through InstallAiScript, with $CF=7 and $0236=0. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and animation state.

32 words, each the animation the actor that is hit answers a blow with: the player's when the enemy hits them (installed with InstallAnimation), the enemy's when the player does (InstallAiScript). Targets: $BCEB, $BCEB, $BCE3, $BCE3, $BCEB, $BCEB, $BCE3, $BCE3, $BD01, $BD01, $BCD3, $BCDB, $BCDB, $BCD3, $BCF3, $BCF3, $BCEB, $BCEB, $BCF3, $BCF3, $BD01, $BD01, $BCE3, $BCE3, $BD01, $BD01, $BCE3, $BCE3, $BCEB, $BCEB, $BCF3, $BCF3.
EnemyResponseAnimations plus 1, the address the instructions at $A4EF and $A4FE read with Y as the index: the high byte of each word of the table, the index counting in pairs from the low byte.

Test whether the selected combat actors overlap. Inputs: X selects an actor and current positions and bounds are valid. Outputs: flags and transient contact state report overlap or separation. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and overlap scratch.

Mark AI scripting active and install a new AI script pointer. Inputs: X is pointer low and A is pointer high. Outputs: $76 is set to one, $62/$63 receive the pointer, $5E/$5A are cleared, A returns zero, and X is preserved. Clobbers: A, N, Z, and AI script state; X and Y are preserved.

Install an AI script without changing the active marker. Inputs: X is pointer low and A is pointer high. Outputs: $62/$63 receive the pointer, $5E/$5A are cleared, A returns zero, and X is preserved. Clobbers: A, N, Z, and AI script state; X and Y are preserved.

Finish installing a The Street AI script when its low pointer byte was stored separately. Inputs: A is the script-pointer high byte and $62 already contains its low byte. Outputs: $63 receives A, $5E and $5A are cleared, and A returns zero; $62 is unchanged. Clobbers: A, N, Z, $63, $5E, and $5A; X, Y, C, V, and $62 are preserved.

16 unsigned lower horizontal bounds. $A599-$A5FD derives index from attack-pose class and selected object/weapon state, then compares separation with these paired limits. $FF slots remain literal bounds; their ordinary-play reachability is open. These are combat-overlap parameters, not graphics.

16 exclusive upper horizontal bounds. $A599-$A5FD derives index from attack-pose class and selected object/weapon state, then compares separation with these paired limits. $FF slots remain literal bounds; their ordinary-play reachability is open. These are combat-overlap parameters, not graphics.

16 unsigned lower vertical bounds. $A599-$A5FD derives index from attack-pose class and selected object/weapon state, then compares separation with these paired limits. $FF slots remain literal bounds; their ordinary-play reachability is open. These are combat-overlap parameters, not graphics.

16 exclusive upper vertical bounds. $A599-$A5FD derives index from attack-pose class and selected object/weapon state, then compares separation with these paired limits. $FF slots remain literal bounds; their ordinary-play reachability is open. These are combat-overlap parameters, not graphics.

Restore an actor's saved mode, derive its facing/pose code, and perform channel-specific follow-up.
Inputs: Actor channel offset X, current heading/mode at $69+X, saved mode at $71+X, and actor state arrays $5D/$65.
Outputs: Copies heading bit 1 to $5D+X, restores $6D+X from $71+X, derives $65+X from restored/current heading; player channel sets $9F=$FF, opponent channel rebuilds state and sets $CF=8.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $5D+X/$6D+X/$65+X, and either $9F or opponent helper/AI state.

Admit and dispatch one active-opponent AI step, or route collision/boundary state to recovery
Inputs: active-enemy sign latch $CB; collision/boundary fields $02B0-$02B2; AI state $CF; timer slot 12; target-minus-one table beginning at $A6D5
Outputs: inactive enemies return; collision/boundary state jumps to recovery at $AA09; admitted normal state dispatches the selected AI handler by stack/RTS
Clobbers: A, X, flags, two stack bytes, and handler-dependent state; Y is preserved until the handler

16 words, one for each state of an enemy's fighting mind from state 0 up, each the address of that state's routine less one: the dispatcher pushes it and returns into it. Targets: $A6F5, $A702, $A76C, $A71B, $A73B, $A7F0, $A924, $A95F, $A964, $A9A7, $A9B4, $A9B5, $A7A3, $AAAF, $0000, $A7CC. State 14's word is $FFFF, which would return to $0000: it is not a routine, and nothing in this load or the engine sets $CF to 14.
AiDispatchTable plus 1, the address the instruction at $A6C9 reads with X as the index: the high byte of each word of the table, the index counting in pairs from the low byte.

Set the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 4 plus its facing $6B shifted right once; this is AI state 0's handler in the table at $A6D5.
Inputs: Current opponent facing $6B.
Outputs: Stores floor(($6B + 8)/2), which is 4 + $6B/2, in $6F and returns.
Clobbers: A and flags; $6F.

Set the Street opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 0 plus its facing through the common tail at $A6FB.
Inputs: $6B is the current opponent facing/direction code.
Outputs: Computes $6F=(2*0+$6B)/2, mode class 0 plus the facing halved, and returns with it stored in $6F.
Clobbers: A, N, Z, C, and $6F; X and Y are preserved.

Set the opponent's action mode. Inputs: A is the mode class (0, 4, 8, an attack class $14-$20, or $24 for defeat) and $6B is the opponent's facing. Outputs: $6F = A + $6B/2, the class plus the facing halved, the same layout as the player's $6D. Clobbers: A, flags, and $6F.

Initialize a timed AI decision state and its random delay.
Inputs: AI option byte $D0 bit 6, tick $E2, current heading $6B, and random source $AE0A.
Outputs: Sets state $CF to 3 or 4, snapshots tick to $0275, stores random delay 0..31 in $CC, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 0 plus the facing halved.
Clobbers: A, flags, $CF, $0275, $CC, $6F, and random-source scratch.

Wait for the AI delay to expire, then enter state 5 with a rebuilt heading/action.
Inputs: Current tick $E2, delay origin $0275, delay $CC, current heading $6B, and helper state.
Outputs: Before expiry returns unchanged; at expiry sets $CF=5, derives and stores a new heading in $6A/$6B, invokes setup $AC31 with X=8, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 8 plus the facing halved.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, and helper scratch.

Face the opponent into the player's current relative quadrant and enter approach state 5.
Inputs: Player high-byte coordinates $54/$55 and opponent high-byte coordinates $56/$57; opponent heading and action fields.
Outputs: Sets AI state $CF=5, stores the quadrant classification returned by $AC19 into both $6B (current heading) and $6A (desired heading), installs direction action class 8 through $AC31 with X=8, sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 8 plus the facing halved through $A6FB, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $6A/$6B/$6F/$CF and helper scratch.

After the timed delay, choose a two-step heading turn, enter state 2, and begin horizontal-travel tracking.
Inputs: Tick/delay fields $E2/$0275/$CC, random source, heading $6B, and opponent X $56.
Outputs: At expiry sets $CF=2, rotates $6A/$6B by +2 or -2 modulo 8, snapshots $56 in $D1, runs setup X=$18, sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 8 plus the facing halved, then continues into the travel tracker at $A76C.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, $D1, and helper scratch.

Track horizontal displacement from $D1, escalate after at least $14 units, and fall back to state 5 when the range test drops below $70.
Inputs: Opponent heading $6B, current X $56, baseline X $D1, tick $E2, and distance helper $ABF7.
Outputs: At sufficient directed displacement sets $CF=$0C, snapshots tick, calls setup X=4, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 0 plus the facing halved; independently, a helper result below $70 resets through the state-5 entry at $A725, which sets $CF=5 and turns $6A/$6B toward the player.
